scenario: [LGRA.9.2.1]'s precedence, observed by which rules fire. A `compile_ok` vector compiles under any grouping, so each rule here is written so the table's grouping and the other one answer differently. One P fact holds a = 1, b = 2, c = 3, t = true and f = false. `or_looser_than_and`: `p.t or p.f and p.f` is `t or (f and f)`, true; grouped as `(t or f) and f` it is false. `and_tighter_than_or`: `p.f and p.f or p.t` is `(f and f) or t`, true; grouped as `f and (f or t)` it is false. `mul_tighter_than_add`: `p.a + p.b * p.c == 7` is `1 + 6`; grouped as `(1 + 2) * 3` it is 9. `sub_left_assoc`: `p.c - p.b - p.a == 0` is `(3 - 2) - 1`; grouped right it is 2. Each wrong grouping has a rule of its own, which `dead_rules_expected` requires never to fire: `mul_grouped_first` (`== 9`) and `sub_grouped_right` (`== 2`). The two Bool cases need no such rule, since their wrong grouping is false and the rule simply does not fire. Agenda order is source order ([LDET.5.4]). Path: the compiler's parser (`dsc.parse`) builds the expression tree, and both runtimes evaluate the tree they are given (libds rete/eval.c, Mercury ds.eval). So a wrong grouping in the compiler shows on both runtimes alike.
rules_ds:
schema P scope logical:
    id: String key
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable
    c: Int mutable
    t: Bool mutable
    f: Bool mutable

rule or_looser_than_and:
    P p where p.t or p.f and p.f
->
    log info "or_looser_than_and"

rule and_tighter_than_or:
    P p where p.f and p.f or p.t
->
    log info "and_tighter_than_or"

rule mul_tighter_than_add:
    P p where p.a + p.b * p.c == 7
->
    log info "mul_tighter_than_add"

rule mul_grouped_first:
    P p where p.a + p.b * p.c == 9
->
    log info "mul_grouped_first"

rule sub_left_assoc:
    P p where p.c - p.b - p.a == 0
->
    log info "sub_left_assoc"

rule sub_grouped_right:
    P p where p.c - p.b - p.a == 2
->
    log info "sub_grouped_right"
